c82964ada_owner_sig_observable.evidence: 1. **Adversary-constructable griefing**: Given any valid on-chain ECDSA signature from an AtomWallet owner (observable after any executed UserOp), an adversary derives the high-s counterpart: `s' = secp256k1_order - s`, `v' = v XOR 1`. The recovered address is identical to the original signer, so the signature appears legitimate until `tryRecover` rejects the high-s value. The adversary can then repeatedly submit griefing UserOps targeting any AtomWallet.

c82964ada_high_s_derivable.meaning: an observer can derive a high-s counterpart (s' = curve_order - s, v' = v XOR 1) recovering the identical signer
c82964ada_high_s_derivable.evidence: `RecoverError.InvalidSignatureS` is triggered by OpenZeppelin's ECDSA library when the `s` component of a signature falls in the upper half of the secp256k1 curve order (high-s signature). While modern wallets following EIP-2 canonical signature rules produce low-s signatures, high-s signatures are technically valid ECDSA signatures. Crucially, any observer of a valid owner signature can derive a high-s counterpart by computing `s' = curve_order - s` — the recovered address is identical, making this a constructable input against any live wallet.
